claims.text: The proposed system is a nanoscale multilayer coating pairing an FCC CoCrFeMnNi-type HEA with a refractory BCC HEA.
The FCC and BCC layers can be suitably matched to form well-defined coherent interfaces with identical nanoscale layer thicknesses.
Sustained loading at elevated temperature progressively lowers the activation barrier for dislocation nucleation specifically at coherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
Lowering the interfacial nucleation barrier produces evolving interfacial dislocation arrays and stacking faults.
Interfacial dislocation arrays and stacking faults facilitate controlled progressive plastic deformation.
Nano-mechanical creep testing can be conducted under sustained load at room temperature, 400 °C, and 600 °C.
In situ TEM creep testing can be combined with high-resolution STEM to quantitatively map interfacial dislocation density during the proposed comparison.
Holding applied stress and film thickness constant isolates the effect of thermal activation at the interface.
The governing structural mediator is the evolution of dislocation arrays and stacking faults localized at multilayer interfaces.
Temperature-driven barrier reduction under steady loading causes a progressive accumulation of dislocations and stacking faults that gradually accommodates plastic strain.
Evolution of the interfacial dislocation network enables smoother plastic flow and balances strength with deformation tolerance.
Elevated-temperature specimens will have a higher and more uniformly distributed density of interfacial dislocation arrays and stacking faults than room-temperature specimens.
The elevated-temperature defect evolution will correlate with smoother creep and lower strain-hardening rates than at room temperature.
At room temperature, the multilayer baseline has limited dislocation activity, greater strain hardening, and less interfacial accommodation of plastic strain.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the nanoscale multilayer structure and interfacial coherency are retained without significant phase transformation.
Significant interface decohesion places the material outside the proposed mechanism's applicable regime.

Failure to observe reproducible temperature-dependent growth of interfacial dislocation density and stacking faults, or failure of that growth to correlate with smoother creep and reduced hardening, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that applied stress is held constant, whereas the intervention and falsification design specify constant-load testing. In nanoindentation creep, constant load does not generally imply constant stress because contact area can evolve during deformation.
